newsitem.title: FRANCE: CIC stands firm on privatisation terms.
newsitem.headline: CIC stands firm on privatisation terms.

text.p: French CIC bank, which is owned by state insurer GAN, said on Tuesday the terms and conditions the government has laid down for its privatisation should be respected.
"The government drew up a file of terms and conditions...I stick by them," CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt told a news conference where he presented the bank's first-half results.
Yoncourt declined to comment on any other aspect of the upcoming privatisation by trade sale.
Yoncourt said the group's asset value including results would stand at around 14.6 billion but was careful not to allow too much to be read into this in terms of the privatisation price.
"I'm talking about the net asset value, not the price of a transaction," he told the news conference.

"This government produced a list of terms and conditions. This includes a certain number of declarations and a number of questions which candidates are asked to answer. When you pose questions it means you are not disinterested in the reply," Yoncourt said.

He noted that the terms and conditions included the bank "maintaining this totally original network operation and position" as a "group of decentralised banks...with national coverage, with this identity as a regional bank."
The CIC comprises 11 regional banks. A government tender for offers for 67 percent of the bank closes on October 7.
